messages:
Mia: heads up — after the telemetry-proxy canary rolled (yesterday ~18:20) a bunch of dashboards are hitting long first-paint on charts, specifically heatmap + timeseries. noticed lots of main-thread longtasks.
Sam: repro steps? can you link a slow trace?
Mia: https://internal.traces/abc123 — open the metric explorer, select 30d, then toggle compare mode. LCP goes up and several 200-400ms tasks show in flame.
Diego: looking at traces — main culprit looks like a new telemetry init path doing synchronous schema inflation in widget bundle. the import moved from console-main -> widget chunk so the widget now eagerly constructs a lot of objects on read.
Anya: ahh — that explains bundle bump earlier too. I saw a +180KB PSDiff for widget chunk in the last deploy.
Sam: can you paste the import stack?
Diego: stack snippet: `TelemetryClient.initSync -> schemaLoader.inflate -> Object.assign(...)` — the init is called during widget render because the module top-level now does `TelemetryClient.get()` instead of lazy factory.
Mia: this is happening only in EU canary (we set telemetry-proxy weight to 20% for EU). US looks fine.
Anya: quick fix: change to lazy getter + dynamic import for the heavy schema. patch is simple: `const getClient = async () => (await import('./client')).get()` and call in useEffect for non-blocking paths.
Sam: we debated this earlier — there's also the internal API change: /api/widgets now returns enriched telemetry metadata which triggered the SDK change. is the enriched payload necessary at render time?
Mia: product wanted the metadata available immediately for annotation overlays. but UX > slight enrichment — perf hit is bigger.
Diego: alternative: keep enriched payload server-side and only hydrate overlays after initial paint. use placeholder until background fetch completes.
Anya: I'll put up a small PR to lazy-init the SDK and move schema inflation off render path.
Sam: +1 to PR. also propose a short rollback of the EU canary to 0% until we patch — reduce user impact.
deploy-bot: deploy started: rollback telemetry-proxy-canary eu -> 0% (initiated by Sam). CI checks running.
Mia: thanks. one more thing — routing policy/quotas: when we rollback the canary we should make sure the telemetry ingestion quota policy doesn't reclassify the traffic and cause billing spikes.
infra-bot: note: if canary weight changes rapidly, some upstream routing caches might cause brief double-sampling; watch ingestion counts for the next 30 min. alerts already set: `telemetry.ingest.rate > 95pct` will page.
Sam: I'll watch the ingestion dashboard and mute noisy alerts if needed.
Anya: PR up: `pr/5421` — it changes top-level telemetry import to lazy getter + moves schema.inflate to postRender job. small unit + e2e tests added.
Diego: running local build now to sanity-check bundle sizes. preliminary: widget chunk drops 160KB after the lazy split.
Mia: awesome. after PR merges, let's canary the fix in EU at 5% before re-enabling full rollout.
Sam: agreed. plan: rollback -> merge PR -> 5% canary for 1h -> monitor LCP, main-thread longtasks, ingestion rates -> escalate if regressions.
Anya: I'll add a console banner for on-call to see the canary status.
Mia: thanks team :heart:
deploy-bot: rollback complete (telemetry-proxy-canary eu -> 0%).
